screens_reviewed: Single route app/reports/[submissionId].tsx captured at three scroll positions (top: overview + submission/context panels + section chart; early: score-by-section bars, score results table, totals; end: section weighting meters, highest/lowest panels, comments grid + sticky footer).
verdict: A dense, well-structured report screen that reads cleanly in dark mode with a clear hierarchy (overview, hero, chart, table, weighting, highlights, comments) and a persistent Share / Back-to-My-Audits footer. The core iPad weakness is that the route never subscribes to the live design system and never uses Tamagui media/breakpoints: it relies on minWidth-driven flexWrap for its multi-column panels, so at this captured width every two-up row collapses to a single stacked column and the large canvas reads as a stretched phone layout. Content is centered via the shared responsive container, so spacing is reasonable, but the screen leaves obvious two-column/master-detail real estate unused.

critical_issues.issue: The screen imports the STATIC `designSystem` (lib/design-system.ts exports it bound to lightColors) and uses `designSystem.colors.*` 76 times, including `bg={designSystem.colors.background}` on the root YStack and ScrollView. It never calls `useDesignSystem()`, so it does not subscribe to the auditor's theme/fontScale/dyslexic preferences. Per the code this screen should paint light tokens (#FBFAF6 bg, #0F1720 text), yet it renders dark in the capture — the rendering and the source disagree, which means theme/contrast on this screen is not actually driven by the palette the rest of the app uses and will not follow live theme switches.
critical_issues.evidence: packs/reports-submissionId.md:19 (`import { designSystem } from "lib/design-system"`), :252/:256 (`bg={designSystem.colors.background}`); core.md:453-460 (designSystem = lightColors) and core.md:501-510 (useDesignSystem is the live hook); dark render visible in all three images
critical_issues.fix: Replace the module-level `designSystem` with the `useDesignSystem()` hook inside the component (and thread tokens into the child components via props or a context) so the screen follows resolvedTheme, fontScale, and the dyslexic font like the rest of the app. Sibling components (YeeStackHeaderTitle, useYeeStackHeaderOptions) already use the hook.

critical_issues.location: InfoPanel rows (XStack flexWrap), HighlightsRow, comments XStack, ScoreResultsTable metric cards
critical_issues.issue: On iPad the screen is a single centered column the full width of the content track. The only 'multi-column' behavior is `XStack flexWrap="wrap"` gated by child minWidth (InfoPanel minWidth 280, CommentBlock 250, MetricCard 150). At the captured width the two InfoPanels (Submission details / Context), the two Highlights panels, and the comment blocks all wrap to one column, wasting the large canvas. There is no use of Tamagui media queries or `layout.isTablet`/`isWideTablet` to force a 2-up (or master-detail) arrangement, so iPad looks like a scaled phone.
critical_issues.evidence: packs/reports-submissionId.md:315 & :541 (InfoPanel minWidth 280, flexWrap wrap), :413 & :837 (comment/highlights XStacks), :902-922 (MetricCard minWidth 150); panels render stacked in images 13 & 15; core.md:939-1052 exposes isTablet/isWideTablet which the route ignores
critical_issues.fix: Drive columns explicitly from `useResponsiveLayout()` (e.g. set InfoPanel/CommentBlock flexBasis to '48%' / '31%' when layout.isTablet, or use Tamagui `$gtSm`/`$gtMd` media props) so the two summary panels sit side-by-side and comments form a 2–3 column grid on iPad instead of relying on minWidth wrap.

improvements.suggestion: The absolute footer uses `paddingHorizontal: layout.screenPaddingHorizontal` while the scroll content is centered with the adaptive gutter from getResponsiveContentContainerStyle. On wide iPad widths the footer buttons can span edge-to-edge while the report column is centered, so Share / Back buttons won't align with the content track above them. Constrain the footer's inner XStack to the same contentMaxWidth and alignSelf center.
improvements.evidence: packs/reports-submissionId.md:462 (footer paddingHorizontal=screenPaddingHorizontal) vs :257 (content uses getResponsiveContentContainerStyle adaptive gutters); core.md:739-769

improvements.location: Report overview (fontSize 30), ReportHeroCard (28), Card titles (20), InfoPanel (18), table/metric text
improvements.suggestion: All font sizes are fixed px literals and the screen does not consume TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE or fontScale (because it never reads useDesignSystem). Body table rows and 12px helper text stay phone-sized on the large iPad canvas. Multiply key sizes by designSystem.fontScale (via the hook) so tablet/accessibility scaling applies here as it does elsewhere.
improvements.evidence: packs/reports-submissionId.md:266 (30), :523 (28), :893 (20), :551 (18); core.md:792 (TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE) and :1089 shows sibling header scaling by fontScale

improvements.suggestion: The Share action opens the native iOS share sheet (Share.share) but the button is text-only. Adding the platform share glyph (or the existing UploadCloud/Send icon) would make the export affordance clearer and more iOS-idiomatic, matching the BarChart3 icon usage in card headers.
improvements.evidence: packs/reports-submissionId.md:196-209 (Share.share), :468-483 (text-only Share button); components/icons.tsx exports Send/UploadCloud

tamagui_notes: design_system_components_used: (none) — the screen hand-rolls every surface (Card, InfoPanel, MetricCard, CommentBlock, ImportanceMeter, ChartBar) with inline YStack/XStack styling and the static designSystem tokens rather than shared ui/* primitives like Badge; consistency with the rest of the app is carried only by the token constants, which are the light set here (packs:862-999, core.md:1551 Badge primitive exists and is unused).

Spacing mixes Tamagui space tokens (gap="$3", p="$4", py="$2.5") with raw pixel literals (ImportanceMeter segment width 22/height 8, ChartBar height 14, minWidth 280/250/150). Acceptable, but the fixed pixel widths are what cause the wrap-to-one-column behavior on iPad rather than a deliberate breakpoint.

The route ignores tamagui.config.ts media entirely (config only spreads defaultConfig.media, core.md:171-173); all responsiveness comes from the JS lib/responsive-layout tokens, and this screen only consumes screenPaddingHorizontal + the content container helper — not isTablet — so no tablet-specific arrangement is triggered.
platform_notes: Safe area: footer paddingBottom uses insets.bottom + 12 (packs:464) and content bottomPadding reserves footerHeight + 24 (packs:258), so the home-indicator area and footer clearance are handled; the cropped top of image 14/15 is a scroll artifact, not a layout bug.

iPad large-canvas verdict: this is a scaled-up phone layout. Content is centered (good) but single-column; the obvious iPad win — Submission details + Context side-by-side, comments as a grid, or a master-detail with the section list — is not implemented because the screen branches on child minWidth wrap instead of layout.isTablet.

Header uses native Stack.Screen with the shared YeeStackHeaderTitle, which DOES adapt to tablet (inline primary | secondary at TABLET_LIMIT 120) — so the navigation header is the one part that is genuinely iPad-aware (packs:1086-1156).
Tap targets: footer Buttons rely on Tamagui Button default height (no explicit height), flex:1 each — comfortably >44pt wide; fine for thumb/tap on iPad.
not_assessable: Why the screen renders dark while the source uses static light tokens cannot be settled from the pack alone — it may be a capture-harness theme override, a Provider-level repaint, or a stale token path; runtime inspection is needed to confirm whether contrast is actually AA-correct in this dark render.

Whether the two InfoPanels would sit side-by-side at a wider iPad split-view/landscape width (the capture appears portrait-narrow); the wrap threshold depends on the actual windowWidth at capture time.
Exact contrast ratios of muted text (mutedForeground on surface) in the rendered dark palette — estimated acceptable but not measured.
Loading and offline/error states (Spinner, 'Report unavailable offline', pending-upload card) are not shown in these captures.
score_rationale: Usable with clear problems (5-6 band). The information design, hierarchy, and footer pattern are solid and ship-quality, but two real issues hold it back: the screen never subscribes to the live design system (uses the static light token set, contradicting the dark render and breaking live theme/fontScale/dyslexic support), and it makes no genuine iPad adaptation — relying on minWidth flexWrap so the large canvas renders as a single stretched-phone column with unused two-column/master-detail real estate.
